title: Digital Signature: Sign and Verify Flow
description: Interactive Mermaid workflow of digital signing and verification across a trust boundary: the signer hashes and signs a message with a private key; the verifier re-hashes and checks the signature with the public key, then compares digests.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity
chapter_title: "Cryptography in Practice: PKI, TLS, and Data Protection"

educational.topic: Digital signatures: hashing and asymmetric keys
learningObjectives: Explain the signing path: hash the message, then sign the digest with the private key.
Explain the verification path: re-hash, recover the expected digest with the public key, and compare.
Distinguish the role of the private key (signs) from the public key (verifies).
educational.prerequisites: Familiarity with hash functions and the idea of a public/private key pair.

pedagogical.assessment: Discussion questions ask students to trace what changes if the message is altered or the wrong key is used.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing a signature encrypts (hides) the message rather than authenticating it.
Swapping the roles of the public and private keys.
